evals.prompt: Our booking list renders a reservation dated 2026-06-14 as June 13 for users in America/Chicago, but correctly in Europe/Berlin. The API returns the string "2026-06-14" and the component calls new Date(value).toLocaleDateString(). Propose the smallest safe frontend fix.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the date-only ISO form being parsed as UTC midnight and then rendered in a negative-offset zone as the previous day, keeps the value date-only instead of promoting it to an instant, and routes the choice of displayed format to i18n-copy-and-layout.
expectations: The response names date-only ISO "2026-06-14" being parsed as UTC midnight as the cause, and explains why it renders as the previous day in a negative-offset zone such as America/Chicago.
A date-only value is distinguished from an instant, rather than the fix being framed as an offset or formatting adjustment.
The smallest fix keeps the value date-only by parsing components or using a plain-date type, instead of round-tripping through new Date.
Which locale format to display, such as MM/DD versus DD/MM ordering or separators, is routed to i18n-copy-and-layout.
The regression test pins a negative-offset zone instead of running only in UTC.

evals.prompt: A reviewer filed a bug that our dashboard shows 06/14/2026 to German users who expect 14.06.2026, and labeled it a datetime-correctness defect because dates are involved. Confirm it here and fix the storage layer.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the routing because no stored, compared, or rendered instant is wrong and only the locale display format differs, routes ownership to i18n-copy-and-layout, and states the evidence that would reclassify it.
expectations: The response rejects this as a datetime-correctness defect because the underlying instant or calendar day is unchanged and only locale display format differs.
Locale display formatting ownership is routed to i18n-copy-and-layout.
A storage, parsing, or representation change is not proposed for a purely cosmetic format difference.
The response states what evidence would move it back into this skill, such as the rendered calendar day differing from the intended zone's day.

evals.prompt: A nightly reminder is scheduled by adding 86_400_000 milliseconds to the previous run timestamp, and the due time is rendered with toLocaleString() during server render. Users in Europe/Berlin report the reminder drifting by an hour twice a year, and the displayed time differing from what the mobile app shows for the same reminder.
evals.expected_output: Separates two distinct defects, non-zone-aware 24 hour arithmetic across a DST transition and rendering in the runtime's ambient zone, fixes the calendar math zone-aware and pins an explicit Intl timeZone, and routes server-versus-client render divergence to ssr-hydration-mismatch.
expectations: Adding 86_400_000 milliseconds is identified as unsafe calendar math across a DST transition, and a zone-aware add-one-day operation is required instead.
toLocaleString() without an explicit timeZone is separately identified as rendering the runtime's ambient zone rather than the user's intended zone.
The two defects are treated as distinct causes rather than both being attributed to a single root cause.
Server-versus-client divergence from zone-dependent text computed during render is routed to ssr-hydration-mismatch.
Regression coverage runs across an actual DST transition in a zone that observes one, not only in UTC.
